findings.title: False nonconstant-column preservation in Corollary4.10
hypotheses_checked: F(n,m)=f_p(m+1) has column values1,2 at m0,1
For every integer line j,i, normalize by p^min(v_p(j),v_p(i+1)), using constant1 for the zero line; all regulated points match Definition4.5
findings.decisive_evidence: F(n,pm)=f_p(pm+1)=1 for every integer m. All Tetris columns are constant. Exact finite checks151650 regulated digits plus6001 Tetris samples supplement the all-integer analytic proof.
findings.core_dependency: The corollary is the stated nonconstant-column preservation guarantee for the core Theorem4.9 recursion, feeding Theorem4.6 and the decorated reduction.
findings.impact: Unrestricted named guarantee is false. The actual normalized induction subcase survives; no counterexample to the main theorem is claimed.
findings.repair_verification: Require F(n,m)=pi_p(bm) on p-units with b unit. The noncircular r1 coefficient comparison preceding Cor4.10 gives B1=b modp, and Theorem4.7 then makes the Tetris image nonconstant. Equation4.23 has this normalization once P3 is repaired.
findings.severity_basis: False core preservation assertion with exact admissible counterexample; surviving restricted use is documented separately rather than downgrading for a short repair.

independent_acceptance.source_claim: PDF p.25 Corollary 4.10 quantifies over every nonconstant-column S_{p,N} solution, without the prior normalization (4.11). Definitions 3.1 and 4.5 require all integer nonvertical lines and only points of valuation at most one.
independent_acceptance.independent_argument: For p=53,N=2809,F(n,m)=f_p(m+1), the zero line j=i+1=0 has constant witness 1. Otherwise divide (j,i+1) by its common p-power; at least one normalized coefficient is a unit, and the last digit agrees, including the assigned value at zero. Every column takes values 1 and 2, whereas F(n,pm)=1 for every integer m. This is an all-line analytic proof, not an inference from the finite test.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_repair: Proposition 3.4 preserves being a solution only. The earlier normalized case F(n,m)=pi_p(bm) for p not dividing m does survive: the p.23-24 comparison yields B1=b modulo p without using Corollary 4.10; Theorem 4.7 then gives nonconstant Tetris columns. Equation (4.23), after P3's precision repair, supplies that hypothesis.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Major retained for a false named core preservation guarantee used in the structural recursion. The actual normalized invocation can be recovered. No counterexample to Theorem 4.6 or Theorem 1.3 is claimed.

findings.title: Exceptional-row freedom invalidates Remark4.11 bijection; related zero and digit identities

items: p27 increment display and h_nm display

hypotheses_checked: F_k=f_p(m) for m!=0 and F_k(n,0)=k for k1,2
Each zero row uses constant affine witness k; roots of nonzero lines have infinite valuation and are excluded
Both functions have nonconstant columns and the same (c,D,E)=(1,0,0) away from roots
findings.decisive_evidence: Distinct admissible F1,F2 share the triple. Also f53(53)-f53(52)=2 !=1 mod53 despite both arguments nonzero; r1,m1,h2 gives3 rather than printed1; f53(0)=1 differs from f53(2)f53(0)=2.
findings.core_dependency: Theorem4.6 explicitly excludes roots; Section5 needs existence, not a bijection or these erroneous uniqueness identities.
findings.impact: False extra classification claim and local identities, without removing the existential representation used by the reduction.
findings.repair_verification: Retain uniqueness of parameters from F by affine comparison of unit residues and induction on root digits; do not infer F at zeros. Restrict increment to unit arguments, use h+h_nm only when h is not congruent to -h_nm modulo p (exclude the entire residue class), and restrict factorization to nonzero arguments.
findings.severity_basis: Extra assertions not required by the main proof; no demonstrated central damage from their removal.

independent_acceptance.source_claim: Remark 4.11 pp.26-27 upgrades parameter uniqueness to a bijection and gives the increment and h-shift displays. Theorem 4.6(ii), p.16, explicitly excludes the affine zero locus; p.17 factorization uses the nonzero multiplicative identity outside its domain.
independent_acceptance.independent_argument: F_k=f_p(m) off m=0 and F_k(n,0)=k for k=1,2 are distinct admissible nonconstant-column solutions. On the zero line choose witness k; on any other line normalize (j,i), and every root has infinite valuation and is excluded by Definition 4.5. Both yield (c,D,E)=(1,0,0) off the root. The increment at 52 to 53 is 2 rather than 1 modulo 53, and the h-shift and zero-factor examples have the stated discrepancies.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_repair: Parameter uniqueness from F remains provable by comparing affine forms off at most two root residues and inducting on root digits, using columns 0 and 1. It does not determine F on actual roots. The corrected h formula is c*pi_p(h+h_nm) only when h is NOT congruent to -h_nm modulo p. The old report's exact-equality wording was narrowed to that residue-class condition. At h_nm=1,h=52,p=53, the actual last digit is 1 but the linear residue is 0, although h is not exactly -1. General validity follows from factoring p^(r-1) and requiring a unit; 836 finite checks merely corroborate it.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Minor retained: Section 5 uses existence of the root-excluding representation, not the false bijection or erroneous uniqueness displays. The report correction changes the repair domain, not the finding or severity.
independent_acceptance.report_correction: The exclusion is the entire residue class h=-h_nm mod p, not just exact equality.

findings.title: Insufficient modulus in essential p-adic normalizations
hypotheses_checked: F=f_p(m+p^r) is an admissible nonconstant-column Sudoku solution
A0,B1,Cp^r and D=E=0 meet the stated congruence modulo p^r
m=p^r is in the claimed valuation<=r range
findings.decisive_evidence: Original digit f_p(2p^r)=2; claimed normalized digit f_p(p^r)=1. Independent exact execution for r1..4. This refutes the inference from the stated modulus, not the existence of a better choice.
findings.core_dependency: Precision through valuation r is required for every Theorem4.9 induction stage and for reverse Proposition5.2 domino extraction.
findings.impact: The stated congruence does not justify the core normalization at its boundary. Existence conclusions are not disproved.
findings.repair_verification: Choose D=-A/B,E=-C/B modulo p^(r+1), and CRT modulo both p_l^(r_l+1). Dividing a congruence by p^k for k<=r preserves the unit residue; all required choices exist because B is a unit and the primes are distinct.
findings.severity_basis: Demonstrated invalid inference tied directly to the core recursive and reduction calculations. Explicit repair and preserved existence are separate from severity.

independent_acceptance.performing_role: current primary acceptance assistant; bounded native read-only cross-checks separately attributed
independent_acceptance.source_claim: The printed congruences on p.25 before (4.23) and p.30 before (5.1) are modulo p^r and p_l^{r_l}, but their last-digit conclusions include valuation r or r_l. The primary directly viewed both source images to exclude OCR error.
independent_acceptance.independent_argument: The admissible shifted solution f_p(m+p^r), with A=0,B=1,C=p^r,D=E=0, satisfies the stated congruence but gives 2 rather than 1 at m=p^r. The all-line normalization argument applies to the shift. This refutes the sufficiency of the stated congruence, not the existence of better D,E.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_repair: For a unit B choose D=-A/B and E=-C/B modulo p^(r+1). The difference has valuation greater than r, so at every valuation k<=r the unit residue after division by p^k is unchanged and both arguments are nonzero. Distinct-prime CRT gives the two strengthened congruences, including r_l=0 where the required modulus is p_l rather than 1.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Major retained for the invalid boundary-precision inference in the structural induction and reverse Proposition 5.2. The stronger congruence repairs these uses without changing board width or disproving the existence theorems.

findings.title: Cross-prime unit factors missing from reverse domino reduction

items: p32 affine extrapolation and level-one comparison

hypotheses_checked: Singleton domino alphabet and both diagonal relations, constant decoration
Canonical solution F=(f53(m),f59(m),w) meets all decorated line constraints by separate normalization and CRT
r=(1,1),s=(0,1),j59,c1,n1 and column53 all in range
findings.decisive_evidence: F1(1,59)=6 !=1 and F1(53,59*53)=6 !=1. Actual coefficients are lambda1=c*59^s2 mod53 and lambda2=c*53^s1 mod59.
findings.core_dependency: These coefficient identities are the core extraction of w's valuation dependence and adjacent domino relations in Proposition5.2, leading to Theorem3.2 and Theorem1.3.
findings.impact: Printed core calculation false on a valid decorated solution. Corrected calculation restores both needed valuation transitions; main undecidability not refuted.
findings.repair_verification: Extrapolate a=lambda_l,b=0 modp_l; unit factors preserve CRT surjectivity. At p1*n compare lambda1*n with a*n+b/p1, obtaining b=0 modp1^2; valuation pairs(0,0),(1,0) recover horizontal relation, and symmetrically vertical. Use zero-based n<N/p1.
findings.severity_basis: Exact false identity in a central reduction, not downgraded because replacement unit factors preserve the qualitative endpoint.

independent_acceptance.performing_role: current primary acceptance assistant; bounded native read-only cross-checks separately attributed
independent_acceptance.source_claim: After j=p1^s1*p2^s2, the last display on p.31 claims F_l(n,jn)=pi_{p_l}(c*n); p.32 repeats that coefficient in the level-one comparison. In (5.1), c is fixed before s varies.
independent_acceptance.independent_argument: Take the singleton domino alphabet with both self-relations and F=(f53(m),f59(m),w). For each nonzero line, divide the coefficients by their common prime power separately and choose a common integer witness modulo 53^2 and 59^2 by CRT; the zero line has witness 1 and constant decoration. Both digit columns vary. At r=(1,1),s=(0,1),j=59,c=1,n=1, the first digit is 6, not 1; at column 53 it is again 6. All columns used are inside N=9778129. The line domain is the consistent 0..N-1 domain of Definition 3.1 and (5.2), not the obvious shifted index typo in Definition 5.1.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_repair: The correct units are lambda1=c*59^s2 mod53 and lambda2=c*53^s1 mod59. Their nonvanishing gives a=lambda_l,b=0 mod p_l by affine extrapolation. Multiplication by these units preserves CRT surjectivity of digit pairs. Comparing at p1*n on 0<=n<N/p1, with s1+1<=r1, gives b=0 mod p1^2 and witness valuation pairs (0,0),(1,0); the vertical argument is symmetric. Thus the adjacent domino relations survive. The standalone equivalence about equal last digits needs equal finite valuations, which its actual application supplies.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Major retained for the false core coefficient calculation in the reverse domino reduction. Proposition 5.2 feeds Theorem 3.2; p.12 explicitly combines Theorems 3.2 and 3.3 for Theorem 1.3. Corrected units recover the checked transitions; no false main theorem is asserted.

findings.title: Proposed sheaf topology is not closed under unions
hypotheses_checked: Two adjacent vertices s,t and their domino edge
U_{s}={s} and U_{t}={t} are in the specified family
Any U_Omega containing exactly these vertices must also include their edge
findings.decisive_evidence: Union{s,t} is not any U_Omega, because U_{s,t} contains the edge. Exact two-vertex finite topology check confirms union failure.
findings.core_dependency: Remark explicitly says the sheaf viewpoint is not used later.
findings.impact: The proposed topology and universal stalk identification are false locally; no central reduction depends on them.
findings.repair_verification: Use opens S union D with any edge set D having endpoints in S. Sections impose only included edge relations and glue. Vertex stalks are W, edge stalks are allowed relation pairs.
findings.severity_basis: Unused mathematical sidebar, with a direct local counterexample.

independent_acceptance.performing_role: current primary acceptance assistant; bounded native read-only cross-checks separately attributed
independent_acceptance.source_claim: Remark 2.4 p.8 calls precisely the sets U_Omega the open sets, not merely a basis; p.9 identifies all stalks with W and states that the viewpoint will not be used later.
independent_acceptance.independent_argument: For adjacent vertices s,t, U_{s} and U_{t} are singleton open sets, but their union lacks the forced edge in U_{s,t} and is not in the printed family. Thus union closure fails.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_repair: The generated incidence topology permits S together with any edges whose endpoints lie in S. It is closed under arbitrary unions and finite intersections; sections label vertices and impose only the included edge relations, so compatible sections glue. Minimal vertex neighborhoods yield stalk W, whereas minimal edge neighborhoods yield the corresponding allowed-pair relation. Reading the original family as generators would repair the topology, but that is not the printed assertion.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Minor retained: a substantive error in an explicitly unused mathematical sidebar, with no demonstrated central dependency.
